issue.title: Store launch: App Store + Play submission readiness
issue.body:
Tracking issue for everything that blocks submitting Splotch to the App Store and Google Play. Children's-audience compliance, store policy, and review readiness.

The work is attached below as **sub-issues** — GitHub tracks completion on this issue, so there's no checklist here to go stale. Everything also carries [`area:store-launch`](https://github.com/kylemit/splotch/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3Aarea%3Astore-launch) so it stays findable from search.

## Where this came from

An adversarial pass over the shipped surfaces against current Play and App Review policy — reading the running code rather than the checklists in the `mobile` skill, which are unusually thorough and mostly hold up. Twelve findings, deduplicated across the two stores; six of them hit both.

## Already fixed

Four landed together on `claude/app-store-guidelines-dedup-eruayu`:

- **Admin console is web-only and unlinked.** A five-tap gesture on the version string revealed a link to a token-minting console — the shape Play's Deceptive Behavior policy and App Review 2.3.1 are written against. The gesture, the persisted reveal flag, and the prerendered `/admin/native` page (which shipped inside both native bundles) are gone.
- **Real build-time route exclusion.** A route's `prerender` flag drops only its HTML; its JS chunk still ships, so `/android-beta` put Google Play URLs inside the `.ipa` (App Review 2.3.10). `web/nativeExcludedRoutes.ts` blanks the module source, and `scripts/check-native-bundle.mjs` fails `build:cap` if a forbidden host survives.
- **Trademarked coloring-book list removed.** `web/static/coloring/COLORING-BOOK.md` is served from `static/`, so it was copied into both native bundles; under a heading titled IP it named Frozen, Bluey, Paw Patrol, Spidey, Mickey Mouse, Disney Princesses and Gabby's Dollhouse. No branded artwork ever shipped, which made `store-assets/README.md`'s claim that the books "include Bluey and Frozen pages" both stale and misleading.
- **iOS privacy manifest added.** No `PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy` existed, so upload would fail ITMS-91053 before review began.

## Ordering

Two are upstream of most of the rest:

- the **parental gate** contains the links-out, the key entry, the feedback form, and the BYOK flow in one change
- the **provider decision** may remove the free-tier BYOK path entirely, which would moot part of the BYOK question

The **privacy reword** is downstream of nearly everything — the gate, the provider, the feedback destination, and whether reported images are retained all change what it has to say. Doing it last means bumping `LAST_UPDATED` once.

## Submission-time steps (not code, so not sub-issues)

- [ ] Supply a working, non-expiring **access code** in App Store Connect → App Review notes and Play Console → **App access**, with the exact steps to reach the AI feature. Without it the feature is untestable.
- [ ] In review notes, state that the AI prompt is server-built from a closed style enum (`buildPromptForStyle` + `STYLE_SUFFIXES`) and the child never types free text — this bounds the input space in a way most AI apps' isn't, and it's the strongest argument available on the AI-content questions.
- [ ] Answer both content-rating questionnaires from what actually ships, and confirm the Data safety form and the privacy nutrition label agree with `/privacy` and with `PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy`.
- [ ] Re-check `store-assets/STORE-LISTING-IOS.md`'s pre-committed answers ("Data not collected for everything", "no UGC sharing, no web access") once the sub-issues land — several are currently false.

## Related, not blocking

- Issue 708 — reduce how many `target="_blank"` links exist in the native bundle. Complementary to the gate: fewer links to gate.
- Issue 596 — native-bundle boundary test. `scripts/check-native-bundle.mjs` now covers a slice of this (forbidden hosts in built output), so that issue should be narrowed rather than closed.
- Issue 212 — "Share a Masterpiece" would *add* a sharing surface and re-open the 1.2 UGC questions this set is closing. Worth sequencing after launch.
